slides.title: Start in the lab directory
slides.lead: Relative paths are interpreted from your current working directory.
points: requirements.txt is here; ../dist is one directory up
imu_artifacts is created here for Lab 9.5
Use Ctrl+C to stop a lab; close competing serial tools
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Create an isolated Python environment
slides.lead: Use Python 3.11 for the course’s compiled SDK wheels.
points: py selects Windows Python; -3.11 selects its version
-m runs the standard venv module; .venv names the destination
Activation changes which Python and installed commands your terminal uses
slides.code:
py -3.11 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# macOS:
# python3.11 -m venv .venv
# source .venv/bin/activate
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Install libraries, then the SDK
slides.lead: Run the next line only after the previous install succeeds.
points: -r reads the requirements file; NumPy computes and Matplotlib plots
TensorFlow runs/trains models; pyserial talks to USB serial
-U upgrades; --no-index avoids online indexes; -f supplies local wheels
Use a wheel for your OS and Python version; Linux has no bundled wheel
slides.code:
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install -U --no-index -f ../dist robotos_edge
python -c "import robotos_edge as rk; print(rk.__version__)"
slides.notes: Separate install lines make failure visible. The inspected checkout contains Windows and Apple Silicon macOS 0.2.2 wheels; a filename alone does not prove runtime compatibility.

slides.title: CLI, API, SDK and firmware
slides.lead: The same system exposes several different interfaces.
points: CLI: robotos detect is a terminal entry point
API: rk.Display.open(...) is a Python call
SDK: installed package containing APIs and command tools
Firmware: board software that streams sensors and applies drawing commands
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Discover and check the board
slides.lead: Detect first; then verify the ws28p IMU stream.
points: detect reports the board model, capabilities and firmware
check-imu: expect about 150 samples in 3 s, 50 Hz, lost 0
At rest, |a| should be near 9.8 m/s²
If missing: use a data cable and close serial monitors/browser connections
slides.code:
robotos detect
robotos check-imu
robotos check-imu --port COM5
slides.notes: The good results are expectations from the lab guide, not measurements made by this deck.

slides.title: Firmware must match the board
slides.lead: Pass --board explicitly when you need to update firmware.
points: ws28p has an IMU; es3c28p has a microphone
The CLI downloads binaries, writes flash, then checks the board
Use the correct detected model; do not flash merely to test a slide
A firmware download needs an internet connection
slides.code:
robotos flash-firmware --board ws28p
# For the other model instead:
# robotos flash-firmware --board es3c28p
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.lead: Configure the source and duration, then copy the command.
points: Commands are generated for the labs/python working directory
--port selects the display board even in replay for 9.3–9.5
Lab 9.2 always analyses files; its common --seconds option is not used

slides.title: How --replay is parsed
slides.lead: None and an empty list mean different things.
points: No flag → args.replay is None: live, except Lab 9.2
Bare --replay → []: use idle, shake, circle, lift CSVs
--replay FILE ... → use the named files
Lab 9.1 reads quickly; display labs replay at 50 samples/s and loop
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Prepare the gesture model
slides.lead: The browser does not train or load the lab’s TFLite model.
points: Quick path: synthetic gestures test the training pipeline
Better path: collect multiple people and sessions
--takes 10 records ten 2 s takes per gesture
model_int8.tflite must exist before running Lab 9.5
slides.code:
robotos-kws train-imu --synthetic --out imu_artifacts
# Or use your own ws28p recordings:
robotos-kws collect-imu --person yourname --takes 10
robotos-kws train-imu --data imu_dataset --out imu_artifacts
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.
